scientific_scope_status: For a nonempty polytope P with vertices in{0,1}^n, let k(P) be maximum Hamming length of an actual edge, zero for a singleton. For every real m-by-n A with Euclidean column norms<=1 and every x in P, the source proposes x in conv{v vertex(P):||A(v-x)||infinity<=54k(P)}. Equivalently a law on vertices has E Z=x and the bound almost surely, with at most n+1 atoms existentially. The law may depend on P,A,x; it is not one distribution for every A. For each additional linear objective c there is a good vertex with c^T v<=c^T x, not an assertion that every atom of one unbiased law has that cost property.
